fullText: This isn't a pill, it's a purge. Here's how the most successful drug on earth turned our vaginas into a wasteland. See, our great-grandmothers didn't own a single feminine wash. They didn't know what pH meant and never thought about freshness because there was nothing to think about. Their body ran a system that had been perfected over thousands of years, acidic enough to kill bad bacteria and protected by the good bacteria maintaining the balance. And that system worked perfectly. Until 1928, when Alexander Fleming accidentally left moldy bacteria in a petri dish and everything changed. Because when he came back, the mold had killed everything around it. And the discovery of penicillin would go on to save 200 million lives. We called them antibiotics, Greek for against life. And they were a miracle. Infections that used to kill millions became minor inconveniences. Surgery stopped being a death sentence. And children survived illnesses that would have buried them a generation earlier. So we used them, a lot. And by the 1950s, doctors were handing them out like vitamins. By the 2000s, the average American had taken dozens of rounds before turning 18. And nobody stopped to think about what against life actually meant inside a woman's body. Because antibiotics kill all bacteria. They don't choose between the bad bacteria causing a throat infection and the good bacteria maintaining pH. They just carpet bomb everything. So good bacteria die along with the bad ones. And the colonies that kept our great-grandmother's systems acidic for thousands of years get wiped out, spiking pH levels and causing odor, discharge, and a breeding ground for more bad bacteria. So over the years, we trained bad bacteria to evolve and resist antibiotics. And in response, they learned to build protective protein layers around themselves called biofilms. And once these slime fortress walls go up, probiotics, soaps, and even antibiotics just bounce right off. So women's good bacteria defense system got nuked. While the bad bacteria that filled the space are sitting behind a layer nothing can touch. So things might feel fresher for a week or so, but then come right back. And this isn't about demonizing antibiotics, but acknowledging what they leave behind. And researchers in Milan found that bromelain, an enzyme from pineapple stems, the same one that makes your mouth tingle when you eat it, dissolves biofilms and exposes what's underneath. And when paired with hardy probiotics like bacillus coagulans, they can actually reach and rebuild. Nuora is a natural probiotic blend that combines bromelain to clear the biofilm with bacillus coagulans to colonize with healthy bacteria. A formula that works with biology, not against it. Because balance shouldn't require a medicine cabinet. Your body was built for this. We just clear the way. So start here. You'll see what I mean.
